items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Stan Getz, Zoot Sims, Al Cohn and Serge Chaloff all died I think from cirrhosis of the liver.

ctx.x: Did some of the fellas that were into that suffer later on? Even if they got over it?

They — Stan Getz, Zoot Sims, Al Cohn and Serge Chaloff all died I think from cirrhosis of the liver. Even though they quit. Even when they quit though, they were all drinking. Stan Getz would drink a fifth of liquor and it wouldn’t bother him like it would the guy who never made that. But they were all straight later on. But I think what happened is it affected them. It stays in your system I suppose. Thank God I never did that, and let me tell you one of the reasons. Two things. I like to laugh. And all the…
It must have been hard for Woody to deal with that.

items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Zoot Sims, Chet Baker’s group... For two months, can you do better than that if you want to play with people?

ctx.x: The question was does Terry Gibbs think that there were good old days in his life? And it seems like almost without exception they were all —

All great. Really okay. There was really something every year that was really great and stuck out you know. And let me tell you, let’s face it, when you get a chance growing up listening to Benny Goodman and Duke Ellington and get to know these people, get to know these people. You know like I’ve been on the scene with the Dream Band one time when Duke Ellington introduced the band, and I didn’t want to follow it, because that introduction was so great that whatever I played, it would be ridiculous. I mean Duke…
Southern, Phineas Newborn, Bud Powell. For two months, can you do better than that if you want to play with people? Who’s left?
